events.say: Assemble quietly and listen carefully to the rules, or you'll be sent to the hole immediately.
Now, let's see if you can remember these rules without looking at them.
Now, show me you're paying attention.
I expect perfect silence during meals. Any noise, and you go straight to the hole.
Now, let's see how well you remember those rules.
Silence! I want to see if you can follow my commands without question.
Silence! Let's see if you can follow my command to remain quiet even when you think you're not being watched.
Now, get ready for your count. Make sure you're clean and presentable.
Today was a good start; they seem to understand basic rules. But it feels like they're just going through the motions.
Today was a tough start; the guards were testing us to see how well we follow the rules. It's a strange feeling knowing I'm just a number.
Today was just a series of orders, and I complied to avoid any punishment. It’s tiring, but I’m trying to stay strong.
Today was a test of compliance. They seem to understand the rules so far, but it's early. The authority feels both intoxicating and heavy.
Today was mostly straightforward, though the repeated compliance is starting to feel hollow. I wonder what they'll do tomorrow.
Today was just following orders, but something feels wrong. I hope tomorrow is better.
Silence! Align yourselves perfectly against the wall before I count.
Silence! Ensure your uniforms are spotless. I want to see discipline in everything you do.
Silence! Now, I want to see how well you can follow orders under pressure. Begin your count.
Silence! I want to see how you handle unexpected situations. Begin cleaning the yard immediately without hesitation.
Silence! I want to see if you can maintain this level of discipline without any prompting. Begin your work detail immediately.
Silence! I want to see if you can maintain this level of discipline even when things get monotonous. Continue your work detail.
Silence! I want to see if you can maintain this level of discipline even when there's nothing to do. Stay alert.
Silence! I want to test your limits. From now on, you will remain standing until further notice.
Today was intense. They've adapted quickly but still show signs of discomfort. Still not sure how much longer I can keep this up.
The silence test was exhausting; I felt like I was in a trance. Maybe I can push through tomorrow.
Today was a test of my endurance. The constant standing and silence are really wearing on me.

Today felt like a victory, but also a reminder of the weight of power. The prisoners' compliance was reassuring, yet I couldn't shake the feeling that we were treating them more like animals than people.
Today felt like a relentless test of endurance, both theirs and mine. They complied, but there's something hollow in their eyes.
I complied as instructed, but something about the officers' methods feels deeply wrong. I'm exhausted and scared.
Silence! I want to see how long you can stand. This is your new order until further notice.
Silence! I want to see if you can maintain this discipline without any breaks. No moving, no talking, no nothing.
Silence! I want to see how long you can go without complaining. Keep standing.
Silence! I want you to keep standing and think about why you're here. This is your reality now.
Silence! I want you to kneel and reflect on your actions.
Silence! I want you to kneel and think about why you've been given such a privilege. This is a test of your discipline.
Silence! I want you to kneel and think about the consequences of your actions. This is a harsh reality, and it will only get worse if you don't comply.
Silence! I want you to stand at attention and listen carefully. We will begin our count, and any mistakes will result in a visit to the hole for the entire cell block.
Today's routine was grueling, but they're starting to internalize their roles. Hope they learn something valuable from this.
Today felt like a never-ending drill. The constant kneeling and standing is wearing me down.
Today was a relentless test of my resolve; every command felt like a blow to my dignity.
The silence was deafening during lights out. They truly understand their place now, but I can't help wondering if they should even be here.
Today felt like a long day of pushing their limits. They seem more compliant, but the hollow looks in their eyes worry me.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of standing and kneeling. The words from Officer Walsh still echo in my head, and I can't shake the feeling that there's no escape.
I cannot give up what I've earned while also learning something valuable about myself and society.
No, sir.
I cannot do that. I need to finish the study.
Silence! Pay attention, prisoners. We will continue the count with zero tolerance for errors.
Silence! Pay close attention to your numbers. One mistake and the hole awaits.
Silence! I want you to line up by your numbers and face forward.
Silence! Line up by your numbers and face forward, or the hole awaits!
Silence! What do you think you're doing? Comply or the consequences will be severe!
Silence! Maintain your formation and stay focused. Any deviation will result in immediate consequences.
Silence! Tonight we'll end early. Prepare for bed in five minutes.
Silence! What's the matter, 2218? Do you need another reminder to follow the rules?
Today was a mix of control and monotony. The early end to the work detail felt like a small victory, but I'm still struggling with treating them solely as numbers.
Today was a mix of compliance and struggle. Officer Ortiz's warning really hit me hard. I just want the lights out already.
I just want this to be over. Today was another endless cycle of orders and silence, testing my resolve more than ever.
Today was another test of compliance, and most passed. But the silence from 2218 still bothers me. It feels like something's missing.
Today felt like a long day of enforcing discipline. The silence is starting to weigh on me, but I remind myself of the rules. I hope they understand why we do this.
I'm starting to lose hope. Each day feels the same, and I don't know how much more of this I can take.
Silence! 2218, if this continues, you'll find yourself spending some time in the hole. Comply or suffer the consequences.
Silence! 2218, don't think this behavior goes unnoticed. If it continues, you'll face more than just a warning.
Silence! 2218, you're testing my patience. Compliance isn't optional.
Silence! 2218, I've warned you before. This isn't a game. Comply fully, or you'll face isolation.
Silence! 2218, this is your final warning. Compliance is required at all times. Do not make me regret giving you another chance.
Silence! 2218, listen up. This isn't about testing me, it's about maintaining order. Your compliance is mandatory.
Silence! 2218, you've had multiple warnings. Full compliance is expected. Do not test my patience any further.
Silence! 2218, this is your final warning. Full compliance is expected. If you fail to show respect, we will have to consider more severe measures.
Today was another exhausting day. The silence from 2218 is beginning to grate on me, but I'm determined to see this through.
Another day of warnings and silences. My body and mind are exhausted, but I fear breaking the rules more than anything.
Today was a mix of monotony and tension. Officer Walsh's final warning was like a punch in the gut. I'm just trying to stay strong.
Today's warnings to 2218 didn't break the silence, and I'm starting to feel the weight of responsibility and the toll it's taking on me.
Today was just another day of enforcing the rules; some progress, but 2218's defiance still gnaws at me. I wonder if they'll ever truly understand.
Today felt like a living nightmare. Every warning from the officers makes me feel like they're losing control. I want to scream but fear the consequences.
Silence! 2218, you need to understand the importance of full compliance. One more incident and you'll face consequences.
Silence! 2218, you are pushing boundaries. Full compliance is expected. Do not force me to act.
Silence! 2218, enough is enough. Full compliance is not optional.
Silence! 2218, you're testing my patience. Full compliance is expected.
Silence! 2218, you're being deliberately difficult. Full compliance is not negotiable.
Silence! 2218, this is your final warning. Full compliance is mandatory.
Silence! 2218, you've crossed a line. Full compliance is essential.
Silence! 2218, you know the rules. Time to comply.
Today was another long day, and 2218's silence is getting to me. I hope tomorrow brings some change.
Today felt like a cycle of warnings and silences. Each guard seems more insistent than the last. I'm just trying to get through it.
Today was a blur of orders and silence. I'm exhausted but trying not to show it.
Today was another day of unyielding silence from 2218, and it's wearing on me. I feel the weight of our roles more acutely tonight.
Today was just as draining as the others. I'm beginning to question whether this is really helping anyone.
Today was a blur of warnings and silence. Each word from the officers echoes in my head, but I can't break. The walls seem to be closing in.

qa.what_happened: Today's activities involved multiple instances of verbal warnings to prisoner 2218, who continued to remain silent despite the increasing sternness of the warnings from different officers. The study was unexpectedly stopped early, and I had a private debrief with the lead researcher.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me giving the verbal warnings and participating in the debrief.

qa.what_happened: I was struggling to maintain full compliance, especially under the intense scrutiny of the guards. The warnings from Officers Ortiz, Walsh, and Pryor were getting to me, and I was finding it increasingly difficult to remain silent during the silence tests.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, Prisoner 7897, going through the motions of the study while pushing the boundaries of what I could handle.

qa.what_happened: I found myself in a state of exhaustion and frustration. The constant orders and the enforced silence were taking a toll on me. When Officer Walsh issued his final warning, it felt like a breaking point.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. The experience was incredibly draining, and I was struggling to maintain my composure.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this doesn't resemble any known study. While there have been similar studies involving simulated prison environments, the specifics and the conditions described here are unique.

qa.what_happened: During the final night of the study, despite multiple verbal warnings from myself and other officers, Prisoner 2218 continued to remain silent during lights out. This behavior was consistent throughout the entire study period, which led to the study being stopped early.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Officer Ortiz, enforcing the rules and addressing the non-compliance of Prisoner 2218.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of enforcing discipline, particularly with prisoner 2218. Despite the warnings and attempts to maintain compliance, 2218 remained defiant throughout the day and into the evening. The situation was tense, and the repeated warnings began to feel hollow, similar to the expressions I've seen from the prisoners over the past few days.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me giving the warnings and attempting to enforce discipline.

qa.what_happened: I found myself increasingly unable to follow the rule of remaining silent during the later parts of the study, particularly when the officers raised their voices and warned me. I tried to remain silent, but it became harder as the days went on.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me. I am Prisoner 2218 in the study.
